rule: Test-retest noise per test (e.g. hinge/squat 3%, DB press 4%, pull-ups 10%, broad jump 3%, 30-min TT 2%, 2k row 1.5%); smaller changes are reported as noise.
summary: Meta-analytic and test-specific data set the scale. 1RM tests have a median CV of 4.2% (range 0.5-12.1%), and an e1RM from a rep-max adds estimation error (one rep at a 5RM is about 3% in Epley). Jump distance has a CV of about 2%, and non-athletes and first trials run about 1.3x higher. Self-paced 5-km and 60-min running time trials have CVs of 2.0% and 2.7%. 2k erg mean power has a CV of 2.0% even in well-trained rowers, so 1.5% for a non-rower's W/kg is too optimistic. Pull-up MDC is about 2 reps, so 10% is reasonable. Proposed: hinge_rm and squat_rm 3 -> 4; row_2k 1.5 -> 2.5; run_tt_30 2 -> 2.5; keep the others (broad_jump 3, pullups 10, db_press 4) and keep flagging the rest as coaching estimates. Then refine each from the athlete's own repeat tests (Hopkins typical error from 2 or more trials). Possibly wrong if: the athlete's repeat tests show smaller within-subject variation than these values.

sources.note: Grgic 2020 (32 studies, n=1595): 1RM CV median 4.2%, range 0.5-12.1%; argues 3% is optimistic for hinge/squat.
Hopkins 2001: jump CV about 2%; constant-power tests 0.9-2.0%; non-athletes 1.3x; first-trial CV 1.3x. Broad jump 3% is reasonable.
2k erg power CV 2.0% (1.3-3.1) in well-trained rowers; the 1.5% row value is too tight.
5-km TT CV 2.0% in trained runners on a treadmill; outdoor field tests are likely noisier.
60-min treadmill TT CV 2.7% (1.8-4.0); a 30-min field TT at 2% is on the optimistic side.
Modified pull-up MDC 2 reps (ICC 0.958), consistent with about 10% at 12-15 reps.
